title: Asked, shouted, thought
goal: Attach quotes and thoughts to other verbs with diye, and say why you did something: “Neredesin?” diye sordu; Unutmayayım diye.

intro.text: *Diye* (literally **saying**) attaches a quote or a thought to verbs like *sormak* and *düşünmek*: *“Neredesin?” diye sordu*. After *-sIn* or the optative, it means **so that**: *Bebek uyanmasın diye sessiz konuştuk*.

vocab.en: saying (after a quote); so that; called
to make a note, to take notes

exercises.question: Which sentence means **“Where are you?” she asked**?

why.1: *Sormak* can't take a quote on its own; *diye* attaches the quote to it.
why.2: *Diye* already contains *demek*: use *dedi* alone, or *diye* with another verb.

exercises.explain: *Diye*, **saying**, attaches a quote to any verb other than *demek*.

accept: diye

reject.why: *Dedi* and *bağırdı* can't both introduce the quote. Attach it with *diye*: *“İmdat!” diye bağırdı*.

exercises.explain: With any verb other than *demek*, a quote needs *diye*.

exercises.prompt: I heard that Selin is moving.
accept: Selin taşınıyor diye duydum.
Selin taşınacak diye duydum.
Selin'in taşındığını duydum.
Selin'in taşınacağını duydum.
Selin [taşınıyormuş|taşınacakmış], öyle duydum.
Ben Selin taşınıyor diye duydum.

exercises.en: I didn't call you so as not to disturb you.

exercises.gloss: let me not forget (before diye: so that I don't forget)
exercises.explain: The optative for **I**: negative *-ma*, buffer y, optative *-a*, buffer y, *-ım*. With *diye*, *unutmayayım diye* means **so that I don't forget**.

exercises.en: We're talking quietly so that the baby doesn't wake up.
exercises.explain: Purpose: the third-person imperative + *diye*: *uyanmasın diye*, literally **saying “let him not wake up”**.

accept: I took my umbrella in case it rained.
I took my umbrella in case it [rains|would rain|was going to rain].
I took my umbrella because it might rain.
I took my umbrella because I thought it [would|might] rain.
I [brought|took] my umbrella in case of rain.
I brought my umbrella in case it [rained|rains|would rain].

exercises.prompt: I made a note so I wouldn't forget.
accept: Not aldım, unutmayayım diye.

exercises.prompt: We left early so as not to be late.
accept: Geç kalmayalım diye erken çıktık.
Geç kalmamak için erken çıktık.
Erken çıktık, geç kalmayalım diye.
[Geç kalmayalım diye|Geç kalmamak için] erken [yola çıktık|ayrıldık].
Biz [geç kalmayalım diye|geç kalmamak için] erken çıktık.

reject.why: For a purpose, *diye* follows the optative: *geç kalmayalım diye*, **so that we aren't late**.

exercises.question: *Hasta diye işe gitmedi.* What does *diye* tell you here?
options: A purpose: so that he would be ill

why.1: A purpose would need the imperative before *diye*, and nobody stays home in order to be ill.
why.2: There is no quote and no verb of speaking here.

exercises.explain: After an ordinary form, *diye* gives a reason as someone saw it: **because (he said) he was ill**.

accept: I wondered whether I had locked the door.
I wondered if I had locked the door.
I wondered [if|whether] I [locked|did lock] the door.
“Did I lock the door?” I [wondered|thought].
I thought, “I wonder if I locked the door.”
I asked myself [if|whether] I had locked the door.

exercises.text: Herkes duy___ diye yüksek sesle okudu.
exercises.en: She read it aloud so that everyone could hear.

accept: sun

reject.why: A purpose takes the imperative: *duysun diye*, **so that everyone hears**. *Duyacak diye* would give a reason.

exercises.explain: *duy-sun diye*: literally **saying “let everyone hear”**. *Herkes* takes a singular verb.

exercises.prompt: Do you know a town called Kaş?
accept: Kaş diye bir kasaba biliyor musun?
Kaş diye bir kasaba biliyor musunuz?
Kaş [adında|adlı|isimli] bir kasaba biliyor [musun|musunuz]?
Sen Kaş diye bir kasaba biliyor musun?
Siz Kaş diye bir kasaba biliyor musunuz?
